examples.en: In winter I always wear thermal underwear when I go out.
I put a thin shirt on over my thermal underwear.
I gave my grandfather warm thermal underwear as a gift.
These thermal underclothes are thin but very warm.
My thermal underwear got too small, so I have to buy new ones.
I also bought two sets of thermal underwear.

explain: '속옷'은 안에 입는 옷 전체를 말하고, 속내의는 주로 추울 때 따뜻하게 입는 속옷이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '내복'이라고 더 자주 말해요.
explain_en: '속옷' means underclothes in general, while 속내의 is mainly the kind you wear underneath to stay warm in cold weather. In daily conversation people more often say '내복'.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 속도감이 있어서 지루하지 않아요.
examples.en: This movie has a fast pace, so it is not boring.

examples.ko: 속도감 있는 음악이라 운동할 때 들어요.
examples.en: It is fast-paced music, so I listen to it when I work out.
I sat in the very front seat to feel the speed.
This game is full of speed, so it is fun.
I was amazed by the sense of speed as the scenery rushed past the window.
The sense of speed is great, but it makes me a little dizzy.

explain: '속도'는 빠르기 자체이고, 속도감은 빠르다고 느껴지는 느낌이에요. 영화, 음악, 게임, 글의 흐름처럼 '속도감 있다/넘치다'로 자주 말해요.
explain_en: '속도' is speed itself, while 속도감 is the feeling of things moving fast. It is commonly used for movies, music, games and writing, as in '속도감 있다' or '속도감이 넘치다'.

examples.en: The speedometer says we are already doing 100 kilometers per hour.
The speedometer broke, so I took it in for repair.
Check the speedometer often when you drive.
I attached a speedometer to my new bicycle.
The speedometer needle keeps shaking.

examples.ko: 속도계에 숫자가 크게 나와서 보기 편해요.
examples.en: The numbers show big on the speedometer, so it is easy to read.

explain: 자동차에서는 속도계가 '계기판' 안에 들어 있어서 '계기판을 봐요'라고도 말해요. 자전거나 운동 기구에 다는 작은 속도계도 같은 말로 불러요.
explain_en: In a car the speedometer sits inside the '계기판' (instrument panel), so people also say '계기판을 봐요'. Small speedometers for bicycles or exercise machines are called by the same word.

examples.en: I wore inner shorts under my skirt.
It is windy, so I need inner shorts for under my skirt.
I bought a pair of winter inner pants.
Even though the inner pants are thin, they are quite warm.
Thanks to the inner shorts, even a short skirt is comfortable.
I worried that my inner shorts might show.

explain: '속옷'은 안에 입는 옷 전체이고, 속바지는 치마나 바지 안에 입는 바지예요. 따뜻하게 하려고, 또는 치마 안이 보이지 않게 입어요.
explain_en: '속옷' is underclothing in general, while 속바지 is a pair of pants worn under a skirt or trousers. People wear them for warmth or so nothing shows under a skirt.

examples.en: Nobody knows the real story behind that person.

examples.ko: 회사 속사정을 알고 나니 이해가 됐어요.
examples.en: After learning the company's inside situation, I understood.
He smiles on the outside, but his real situation is complicated.
I asked whether there was some hidden circumstance.

examples.ko: 남의 집 속사정을 함부로 말하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't carelessly talk about another family's private affairs.
You don't even know the real story, yet you get angry first.

explain: '사정'은 일의 형편 전체이고, 속사정은 겉으로 드러나지 않은 숨은 사정이에요. '속내'는 마음속 생각에 가깝고, 속사정은 처한 형편이나 이유에 가까워요.
explain_en: '사정' is a circumstance in general, while 속사정 is the hidden circumstance not visible from outside. '속내' is closer to inner thoughts and feelings, whereas 속사정 is closer to the situation or reason behind something.

examples.en: That friend just laughs without a care.

examples.ko: 속없는 소리 하지 말고 진지하게 생각해 보세요.
examples.en: Stop saying thoughtless things and think seriously.
My younger sibling is so thoughtless that I worry.
He acted carelessly and ended up disliked by his friends.
That person is immature for his age.
Even when they tease him for being so airheaded, he just laughs.

explain: '철없다'와 비슷하지만 나이에 비해 생각이 얕고 걱정 없이 구는 느낌이 있어요. 반대로 생각이 깊은 사람은 '속이 깊다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is similar to '철없다', but carries the feeling of being shallow in thought and carefree for one's age. The opposite, for a thoughtful person, is '속이 깊다'.

examples.en: I put my wallet in the inside pocket of my coat.
I took a small key out of the inside pocket.

examples.ko: 이 재킷은 속주머니가 두 개 있어요.
examples.en: This jacket has two inside pockets.
Thanks to the inside pocket, I can carry my passport safely.

examples.ko: 가기 전에 속주머니를 한번 확인해 보세요.
examples.en: Check your inside pocket once before you go.
I like that the inside pocket can't be seen from outside.

explain: 옷 안쪽에 달린 주머니라서 소매치기가 걱정될 때 귀중품을 넣어 두기 좋아요. 겉에 있는 일반 주머니는 그냥 '주머니'라고 해요.
explain_en: Because it is sewn on the inside of clothing, it is a good place for valuables when you worry about pickpockets. The ordinary pocket on the outside is simply called '주머니'.

en: hands held up like a trumpet

examples.en: The child cupped his hands around his mouth and called his mom.
On the mountain I shouted through my cupped hands.

examples.ko: 바닷가에서 손나팔을 하고 친구 이름을 불렀어요.
examples.en: At the beach I cupped my hands and called my friend's name.

examples.ko: 손나팔을 하니까 목소리가 더 멀리 가요.
examples.en: When I cup my hands like this, my voice travels farther.
I could see someone far away calling with cupped hands.
The hand trumpet looked funny, but it worked.

explain: 입 앞에 두 손을 모아 소리가 멀리 가게 하는 동작이에요. 보통 '손나팔을 하다'라고 말하고, 악기를 부는 '나팔을 불다'와는 달라요.
explain_en: It is the gesture of cupping both hands in front of your mouth so your voice carries far. People usually say '손나팔을 하다', which is different from '나팔을 불다', where you blow a real horn.

examples.en: The children's mouths dropped open at the magician's hand movements.
The chef's hands move really fast.

examples.ko: 그 할머니는 바느질할 때 손놀림이 부드러워요.
examples.en: That grandmother's hands move smoothly when she sews.

examples.ko: 손놀림을 보니 오래 해 본 사람 같아요.
examples.en: Judging by the way his hands move, he seems experienced.
It's my first time, so my hands are still clumsy.
Please show me the hand movements slowly.

explain: 손을 움직이는 모습을 보고 솜씨를 말할 때 써요. '빠르다, 서툴다, 부드럽다'와 잘 어울리고, 타고난 재주를 뜻하는 '손재주'와는 달라요.
explain_en: Use it when judging skill from how someone's hands move, with words like '빠르다', '서툴다' and '부드럽다'. It is different from '손재주', which means natural manual talent.

examples.en: Before the holiday I'm busy preparing to receive guests.
I cleaned the house for our guests starting this morning.
I bought flowers to welcome our guests.
Our shop is popular because we greet customers kindly.
I bought new dishes to use when we have guests.
Getting ready for guests was easy since the family did it together.

explain: 집이나 가게에서 손님을 받는 일과 그 준비를 모두 말해서 '손님맞이 준비/청소'처럼 많이 써요. '손님을 치르다'는 큰 손님 행사를 힘들게 해내는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It covers both receiving guests and getting ready for them, so phrases like '손님맞이 준비' and '손님맞이 청소' are common. '손님을 치르다' has the feeling of getting through a big, tiring event with guests.

examples.en: I pressed my thumbprint firmly on the contract.
I kept my child's handprint as a keepsake.
I had no seal, so I used my thumbprint instead.
I put the paper with the handprint in a frame.
Grandmother slowly pressed her thumbprint on the document.
The thumbprint smudged, so I stamped it again.

explain: 도장이나 서명 대신 손가락이나 손바닥에 물감이나 인주를 묻혀 찍는 거예요. 문서 용어로는 '지장'이라고도 해요. 아이 손바닥 기념 도장에도 써요.
explain_en: It is a print made with a finger or palm covered in ink or paint, used in place of a seal or signature. In documents it is also called '지장'. It is also used for keepsake handprints of children.

examples.en: This sweater can only be hand-washed.
Lukewarm water is best for hand-washing.
The clothing label says hand wash.
If you hand-wash, clothes get less damaged.
The washing machine has a hand-wash cycle.
After hand-washing, dry it in the shade.

explain: 세탁기를 쓰는 '기계 세탁'과 반대되는 말이에요. 옷 라벨이나 세탁 설명에서 많이 보고, 대화에서는 '손빨래'라고도 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is the opposite of machine washing. You see it on clothing labels and in laundry instructions, and in conversation people often say '손빨래' too.

examples.en: I always hand-wash expensive knitwear at home.
Every weekend I hand-wash my underwear and hang it up.
Dissolve detergent in water and hand-wash wool clothes.
The washing machine broke, so I hand-washed the blanket.
I soaked it in water before hand-washing.
Even if it's a hassle, you must hand-wash so the clothes don't shrink.

explain: '손세탁을 하다'와 같은 뜻이지만 '손세탁하다'로 붙여 말하면 더 간단해요. 편하게 말할 때는 '손빨래하다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It means the same as '손세탁을 하다', but saying 손세탁하다 as one verb is simpler. In casual speech people also say '손빨래하다'.

examples.en: The market vendor carries goods with a handcart.

examples.ko: 할머니가 폐지를 실은 손수레를 밀고 가세요.
examples.en: An old woman is pushing a handcart loaded with scrap paper.
I loaded the handcart full of boxes.
The handcart's wheel came off, so I fixed it.
A handcart passed in front of the construction site.
Even though a handcart is small, it holds a lot of stuff.

explain: 사람이 손으로 밀거나 끄는 작은 수레예요. 일상에서는 '리어카'라고도 많이 말하고, 마트에서 쓰는 것은 '카트'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a small cart that a person pushes or pulls by hand. In daily speech it is also often called '리어카', and the kind you use in supermarkets is called '카트'.

examples.en: How much was the loss caused by this accident?
The company is calculating the amount of loss.
The losses were so big that the shop closed.
I got part of the loss back through insurance.
The farms' amount of loss is not yet exact.
We can't raise the price by the amount of the loss.

explain: 손실을 금액으로 말할 때 쓰고, 뉴스나 회사 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 반대는 '이익'이나 '수익'이에요.
explain_en: Use it when stating a loss as a sum of money; it often appears in news and business talk. The opposite ideas are '이익' (profit) and '수익' (earnings).

examples.ko: 일이 커지기 전에 빨리 손써야 해요.
examples.en: We need to take action quickly before things get bigger.
The illness is severe, so there is nothing we can do.

examples.ko: 친구가 미리 손써 준 덕분에 표를 구했어요.
examples.en: Thanks to my friend taking care of it ahead of time, I got a ticket.
If we don't act now, it will be too late.
The company acted right away, but it was no use.
I didn't know what to do, so I just stood still.

explain: 문제가 생겼을 때 대처한다는 뜻으로, '손쓸 수 없다/손쓸 틈이 없다'처럼 자주 말해요. '손(을) 쓰다'처럼 띄어 쓰기도 하고, '조치하다'보다 말투가 편해요.
explain_en: It means to deal with a problem when one comes up, often in phrases like '손쓸 수 없다' (nothing can be done) or '손쓸 틈이 없다' (no time to act). It can also be written as '손(을) 쓰다', and it sounds more casual than '조치하다'.

examples.en: You should use polite speech to your elders.

examples.ko: 손윗사람이 먼저 수저를 들면 먹기 시작해요.
examples.en: We start eating once the elder picks up their spoon first.
I tend to look after my elders well.
I don't cross my legs in front of my elders.
I get a little nervous when talking with my elders.
I greeted my elder first.

explain: '윗사람'과 비슷하지만 손윗사람은 나이가 위인 사람, 특히 가족이나 친척 관계에서 더 잘 어울려요. 반대말은 '손아랫사람'이에요.
explain_en: It is similar to '윗사람', but 손윗사람 mainly means someone older and fits family and relatives especially well. The opposite is '손아랫사람'.

examples.en: Lots of handprints were left on the window.
I brought a rag to wipe off the handprints.
The screen looks dirty because of the smudges.

examples.ko: 눈 위에 작은 손자국이 찍혀 있어요.
examples.en: There are small handprints pressed into the snow.

examples.ko: 스마트폰 화면의 손자국은 닦아도 또 생겨요.
examples.en: Handprints on a smartphone screen come back even after you wipe them.
I like it because the material doesn't show handprints.

explain: 손으로 만져서 남은 자국이에요. 손가락 무늬를 뜻하는 '지문'과 달라요. 오래 만져서 묻은 때는 '손때'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the mark left by touching something with your hand. It differs from '지문', which means the pattern on your fingertips. Dirt that builds up from long handling is called '손때'.

examples.en: Don't fidget with your hands during class.
The child was fiddling around and knocked over a cup.
He fidgets with his hands when he thinks.
My pen broke because of fidgeting.
I was bored, so I made shadow animals just playing with my hands.
Fidgeting has become a habit and I want to fix it.

explain: 손으로 물건을 만지작거리거나 심심해서 하는 장난이에요. 수업이나 회의 중에 '손장난하지 마'처럼 주의를 줄 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It means playing or fiddling with things in your hands, often out of boredom. You often hear it as a warning in class or meetings, like '손장난하지 마'.

examples.en: I cut my nails short with nail clippers.
Could you lend me your nail clippers?
There is a small pair of nail clippers in my bag.
The new nail clippers cut really well.
I packed nail clippers when I went on the trip.
I needed to buy nail clippers too, but I forgot.

explain: '깎다'에서 나온 말이라 '손톱깎이'로 써요. '손톱깍이'는 틀린 철자예요. '손톱을 깎다'와 함께 알아 두면 쉬워요.
explain_en: It comes from the verb '깎다', so the correct spelling is 손톱깎이; '손톱깍이' is a misspelling. It is easy to remember together with '손톱을 깎다' (to cut one's nails).

examples.en: The kids picked up fallen pinecones in the park.
A squirrel is gnawing on a pinecone.
I made Christmas decorations myself from pinecones.
Lots of pinecones have fallen on the ground.
Pinecones open up when the weather is dry.
I received a single pinecone as a gift.

explain: 여기서 '솔'은 소나무를 뜻해서 솔방울은 소나무의 열매예요. 청소나 칫솔처럼 쓰는 '솔(brush)'과는 소리만 같은 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: Here '솔' means a pine tree, so 솔방울 is the cone of a pine. It is a different word from '솔' meaning a brush, as in toothbrush or cleaning brush; they only sound the same.

examples.en: A cool breeze gently comes in through the window.
A delicious smell is drifting from the kitchen.
Smoke is gently seeping out through the gap in the door.

examples.ko: 책을 읽다 보니 졸음이 솔솔 와요.
examples.en: While reading, I'm getting gradually sleepy.

examples.ko: 빵 위에 설탕을 솔솔 뿌려 주세요.
examples.en: Please sprinkle a little sugar over the bread.
A soft spring breeze was blowing, so I went for a walk.

explain: 바람, 냄새, 졸음이 약하고 부드럽게 계속 오는 느낌이에요. 센 바람은 '쌩쌩'이라고 하고, 말이나 일이 막힘없이 잘되는 것은 '술술'이라고 해서 서로 달라요.

phrases.example: 게임을 하다 보니 재미가 솔솔 나요.
phrases.en: As I kept playing the game, it started getting more and more fun.
phrases.nuance_ko: 처음에는 별로였는데 하다 보니 조금씩 재미를 느끼게 된다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means something wasn't much at first, but you gradually start to enjoy it as you go on.

explain_en: It describes wind, smells or sleepiness arriving softly and steadily. A strong wind is '쌩쌩', and things like speech or work going without a hitch are '술술', so those are different.

examples.en: The scent of pine needles fills the forest.

examples.ko: 엄마는 송편을 솔잎 위에 올려 쪄요.
examples.en: Mom steams songpyeon on top of pine needles.
Pine needles piled up thickly on the ground.
A pine tree's needles stay green even in winter.
Have you ever tried pine needle tea?
When I stepped on the pine needles, they made a crunching sound.

explain: 소나무의 바늘 모양 잎을 '솔잎'이라고 해요. 추석 때 먹는 송편을 찔 때 솔잎을 깔기도 해서 한국 음식 이야기에도 나와요.
explain_en: The needle-shaped leaves of a pine tree are called 솔잎. They are sometimes laid down when steaming songpyeon for Chuseok, so the word also comes up in talk about Korean food.

examples.en: The whole roof was blown away by the typhoon.
He lost every bit of the money he had.
I pulled the tree out entirely, roots and all.
That person took my heart completely.
The thief took the whole safe.

examples.ko: 그 일 때문에 생각이 송두리째 바뀌었어요.
examples.en: Because of that event, my way of thinking changed completely.

explain: '통째로'는 나누지 않고 전부라는 중립적인 말이고, 송두리째는 뿌리째 뽑히거나 다 잃는 것처럼 하나도 남지 않는 느낌이 강해요. 그래서 잃다, 빼앗기다, 뽑다 같은 말과 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: '통째로' is neutral and means as a whole without dividing, while 송두리째 strongly suggests nothing is left, as when something is pulled out by the roots or lost entirely. It pairs well with verbs like 잃다, 빼앗기다 and 뽑다.

examples.en: Pine mushrooms smell wonderful but tend to be expensive.
I received pine mushrooms as a Chuseok gift.
I found pine mushrooms in the autumn mountains.
I tried grilled pine mushrooms for the first time.
The aroma of pine mushrooms spread through the house.
Pine mushrooms are expensive, so I bought only a little.

explain: 가을에 소나무 숲에서 나는 향이 좋은 버섯이에요. 줄여서 '송이'라고도 하는데, '꽃 한 송이'의 '송이'와는 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: It is a fragrant mushroom that grows in pine forests in autumn. People shorten it to '송이', which is a different word from the counter in '꽃 한 송이' (one bloom).

examples.en: Lots of pine caterpillars are stuck to the pine tree.

examples.ko: 벽에 붙은 송충이를 보고 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was startled to see a caterpillar on the wall.
Pine caterpillars gnaw on pine needles.
A caterpillar fell down from the tree.
The pine tree withered because of caterpillars.
Don't touch caterpillars with your hands.

explain: 솔잎을 먹는 털 많은 벌레를 말해요. 굵고 짙은 눈썹을 놀리듯 '송충이 눈썹'이라고 하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is the hairy caterpillar that eats pine needles. People also tease someone with thick, dark eyebrows by calling them '송충이 눈썹'.

examples.en: Mom boiled soup in a big pot.
The pot was heavy, so I lifted it with both hands.
I bought a new cooking pot when I moved.
Steam is rising from the pot.
A big pot is hanging in the yard of the country house.
The longer you use a pot like this, the better it gets seasoned.

explain: '솥'을 조금 투박하고 친근하게 부르는 느낌이에요. 가벼운 금속 '냄비'보다 두껍고 묵직한 그릇을 떠올리면 돼요.
explain_en: It sounds like a slightly rustic, familiar way of saying '솥'. Picture a thick, heavy pot rather than a light metal '냄비'.

examples.en: When I opened the pot lid, steam rushed up.
We grilled and ate meat on a cauldron lid.
The pot lid is still hot, so be careful.
The rice is boiling, so the pot lid is rattling.
The pot lid is heavy and hard to open.
We fried and ate pancakes on a pot lid.

explain: 솥의 뚜껑이고, 뒤집어서 고기나 부침개를 굽는 판으로 쓰기도 해요. 냄비 뚜껑은 그냥 '냄비 뚜껑'이라고 해요.

phrases.ko: 자라 보고 놀란 가슴 솥뚜껑 보고 놀란다
phrases.example: 한 번 크게 다치고 나니 작은 소리에도 놀라요. 자라 보고 놀란 가슴 솥뚜껑 보고 놀란다더니요.
phrases.en: After getting badly hurt once, I jump at the smallest noise. It's true what they say: once bitten, twice shy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 번 크게 놀란 사람이 비슷하게 생긴 것만 봐도 겁낸다는 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb: someone who has had a bad scare gets frightened even by things that merely look similar.

explain_en: It is the lid of a 솥, and people sometimes flip it over to use as a griddle for meat or pancakes. A lid for a regular pot is simply called '냄비 뚜껑'.

examples.en: I propped the door open with a metal rod.
Metal rods are piled up at the construction site.
The metal rod got hot, so I couldn't touch it.
I'm worried because the child is playing with a metal rod.
Bending a metal rod is really hard.
I tied a red cloth to the end of the metal rod.

explain: '쇠'는 철 같은 단단한 금속을 편하게 부르는 말이라 쇠막대기, 쇠망치처럼 여러 말에 붙어요. 체육 기구인 '철봉'과는 달라요.
explain_en: '쇠' is an everyday word for hard metal such as iron and attaches to many words like 쇠막대기 and 쇠망치. It is different from '철봉', which is gym equipment (the horizontal bar).

examples.en: Dad hammered in a nail with an iron hammer.
My uncle took the iron hammer out of the storage room.
An iron hammer is much heavier than a wooden mallet.
I heard the sound of an iron hammer all day.
I almost hurt my hand with the iron hammer.
You must not hit the wall with an iron hammer.

explain: 그냥 '망치'라고 해도 보통 통해요. 쇠망치는 나무 망치와 구별해서 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: Simply saying '망치' (hammer) is usually understood. 쇠망치 is used when you want to distinguish it from a wooden mallet.

examples.en: Iron dust is flying around on the workshop floor.
Lots of iron filings stuck to the small magnet.
I wear a mask so I don't breathe in iron dust.
Iron dust got in my eye, so I went to the hospital.
I swept up the iron dust with a broom and threw it away.
Try collecting the iron filings with a magnet.

explain: '쇠'와 '가루'가 합쳐지면서 사이시옷이 들어가 '쇳가루'라고 써요. 소리는 [쇠까루]로 들려요. 쇠를 깎거나 갈 때 나오는 가루예요.
explain_en: It joins '쇠' and '가루' with a sai-siot (ㅅ), written 쇳가루, and sounds like [쇠까루]. It is the powder produced when metal is cut or ground.
